table.name: car_makers
table.purpose: Lookup table of automobile manufacturers; one row per maker, with its short name, full corporate name, and home country (FK to countries). Referenced by model_list.Maker to assign models to makers.

Country.name: country_id
Country.description: Foreign key to countries.CountryId — the maker's home country (e.g. 2=germany, 4=japan, 7=uk).

FullName.name: full_name
FullName.description: Manufacturer's full corporate name (e.g. 'American Motor Company', 'General Motors', 'Daimler Benz').

Id.name: maker_id
Id.description: Primary key; unique maker identifier, referenced by model_list.Maker.

Maker.name: maker_short_name
Maker.description: Short/lowercase maker name (e.g. 'gm', 'bmw', 'amc'), a compact label for the manufacturer.

table.name: car_names
table.purpose: Maps each car model name (make + model, e.g. 'ford pinto') to a numeric ID, with the manufacturer (brand) extracted separately. Each row is one named car model variant; the ID links to the cars_data table's measurements.

Make.name: car_model_name
Make.description: Full car model name combining manufacturer and model (e.g. 'ford pinto', 'audi 4000', 'honda accord lx'). Despite the column name 'Make', it is not just the brand — it is the full model designation.

MakeId.name: car_model_id
MakeId.description: Primary key: unique numeric identifier (1-406) for each named car model. Referenced by cars_data (its Horsepower column appears to carry this ID, likely a mislabeled foreign key) to link specifications to the model name.

Model.name: manufacturer
Model.description: Manufacturer/brand name (e.g. 'ford', 'chevrolet', 'amc'), despite the column name 'Model'. References model_list.Model, which appears to be the maker/model list.

table.name: cars_data
table.purpose: Per-car technical/efficiency records (classic auto-mpg style dataset): one row per car model-year observation with fuel economy, engine specs, weight and acceleration.

Accelerate.name: Acceleration (0-60 mph time)
Accelerate.description: Time to accelerate, in seconds; lower is faster. Range 8.0-24.8 s, typical ~15.5 s, consistent with 0-60 mph times for 1970s cars.

Edispl.name: Engine displacement
Edispl.description: Engine displacement in cubic inches (cu in): range 68-455, values like 350, 318, 400, 455 match American engine displacements in cubic inches.

Horsepower.name: Engine horsepower
Horsepower.description: Engine horsepower (46-230 hp). Declared VARCHAR but values are integers. The detected join to car_names.MakeId is spurious (statistics-only); horsepower is a measure, not a key.

Id.name: Row identifier
Id.description: Primary key, unique 1-406, one row per car record.

MPG.name: Fuel economy (miles per gallon)
MPG.description: Fuel consumption in miles per gallon, 9.0-46.6, typical ~23. Declared VARCHAR but numeric.

Weight.name: Vehicle weight
Weight.description: Curb weight in pounds (1613-5140 lb), consistent with 1970s passenger cars.

table.name: continents
table.purpose: Lookup table of the world's continents, referenced by the countries table.

ContId.name: continent_id
ContId.description: Primary key; numeric identifier for each continent (1-5). Referenced by countries.Continent.

Continent.name: continent_name
Continent.description: Name of the continent: africa, america, asia, australia, europe.

table.name: countries
table.purpose: Lookup table of countries (15 rows), each with a name and the continent it belongs to; referenced by car_makers to indicate a maker's home country.

Continent.name: continent_id
Continent.description: Foreign key to continents.ContId; identifies the continent the country belongs to (1=america, 2=europe, 3=asia, 4=africa, 5=australia).

CountryId.name: country_id
CountryId.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each country. Referenced by car_makers.Country.

CountryName.name: country_name
CountryName.description: Unique lowercase name of the country (e.g. germany, japan, uk, new zealand).

table.name: model_list
table.purpose: A catalog of car models, each row linking a model name to its manufacturer (car maker). Serves as the master list of models referenced by car_names.

Maker.name: maker_id
Maker.description: Foreign key to car_makers.Id, identifying the manufacturer of the model (e.g. 4 = General Motors, 13 = Daimler Benz).

Model.name: model_name
Model.description: The model/make name of the car (e.g. 'buick', 'mercedes-benz', 'opel'). Values look like brand names rather than specific model names; referenced by car_names.Model.

ModelId.name: model_id
ModelId.description: Primary key of the table; unique numeric identifier for each model, range 1-36.
